description: Every pin in the repository, proposed as one weekly pull request, sitedrift, Astro and each major on their own, security fixes at once.

vulnerabilityAlerts.description: A fix for an advisory GitHub reports opens at once, outside the schedule and the release-age hold.

packageRules.description: config:best-practices holds npm releases three days through security:minimumReleaseAgeNpm, a package rule a top-level value does not reach; npm gets the same 7 days as everything else.
Joe's own packages ship from his repositories, so their release is the change being made: no hold.
Node's security releases carry no package advisory for the alerts to see, and they ship from the Node project's own release process, not an npm publish: no hold.
Everything short of a major moves together, digests included, so a week's updates are one pull request.
Astro and its integrations release together and are tested together.
The e2e job runs in Playwright's image, whose browsers serve only the @playwright/test release of the same version, so the two move in one pull request, majors included.
sitedrift is bundled into the production edge functions, so it comes alone and is merged by hand.
wrangler stays on the release the Cloudflare adapter's Vite plugin pins, so it moves by hand with the adapter; checks:repo-policy fails while two copies are installed (docs/Dependencies.md).
Held at TypeScript 6: the audits and Astro's language tools call the compiler API that TypeScript 7 does not ship (docs/Dependencies.md).
@types/node and npm follow the Node major in mise.toml, so their majors move with a Node major (docs/Dependencies.md).

customManagers.description: The mise release CI installs and every machine is held to, which min_version names; mise's own manager reads only the tools.
The Python packages the font task runs through uvx, pinned in the task itself.
Runner labels a job takes from its matrix (`os:`); the github-actions manager reads only `runs-on:`.
The Renovate release checks:renovate validates this file with, pinned in the task itself.
